To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the right hemisphere is involved in the integration of visual and proprioceptive guidance to produce well-coordinated hand-foot movements; (2) the right hemisphere does not play a role in producing well-coordinated movements without visual guidance; (3) visual guidance does not increase activation of the right hemisphere during passive viewing of a visual stimulus; (4) the right hemisphere plays a role in visuo-motor integration during hand-foot coordination, but not during foot-hand coordination.
visual guidance modulates hemi-spheric asymmetries in motor control during a hand-foot coordination task.
the right hemisphere plays a major role in integrating visual guidance with proprioceptive feedback to guide movements in the presence of visuomotor conflict.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the neural basis of visuospatial integration during a complex motor task and shows that the right cerebral hemisphere is involved in the processing and control of visuospatial information when it is integrated with proprioceptive information during motor coordination.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the functional lateralizations of the hemispheres are not hard-wired but are modulated by task demands.

the lateralization of visuomotor networks depends on the type of task performed and the availability of visual guidance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the functional lateralized network of the right hemisphere is not only involved in processing visual or spatial information, but can also be recruited to integrate such information with proprioceptive information to perform complex motor tasks.
the lateralization of brain activity during motor coordination is highly task-dependent and that visual guidance can modulate the functional hemispheric asymmetry of visuomotor circuits.
